text:
sqlpipe moves rows from Postgres to S3 in three stages.

The reader process opens a connection to Postgres and streams rows in batches. Each batch holds a fixed number of rows. The reader sends the batch to the converter.

The converter turns each batch into a Parquet row group. It applies the Parquet schema and compresses the column data. The converter groups row groups into an output object.

The uploader writes the object to S3 as a multipart upload. Each part is one HTTP request. If a part fails, the uploader sends it again. The number of retries is limited. When all parts are complete, the uploader closes the multipart upload. S3 then makes the object available.

The three stages run at the same time. The reader can read batch 3 while the uploader writes batch 1. A queue connects each stage to the next stage. If one stage is slow, the queue fills and the stage before it stops.
